## Yes — demand exceeded the contract on 16 June

**Peak:** 1324.4 kW at 08:15, which is 6% over the 1250 kW contract [data: get_demand].

**Two intervals breached the contract:**
- 08:00 → 1307.1 kW (57 kW over) — up to NT$5,106 penalty [data: list_detections]
- 08:15 → 1324.4 kW (74 kW over) — up to NT$6,652 penalty [data: list_detections]

**Cause:** A simultaneous start of 10 machines (805 kW rated) within 3 minutes between 07:57 and 08:27 — the Monday-morning start-up spike (scenario S2) [data: list_detections]. The demand jumped from ~310 kW before 07:00 to 1324.4 kW at 08:15 [data: get_demand].

**Penalty basis:** Demand above contract is billed at 2× the contract price up to 10% over, and 3× beyond [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-04_glossary.md#EM-04 Glossary > Billing and demand terms > Exceedance].

## Why reflow ovens must be OFF, not standby

A reflow oven in standby still draws **36% of its 70 kW rating = 25.2 kW** for as long as it stays on, which is a large, wasteful load while the line produces nothing (idle energy). A properly switched-off oven uses only about 340–350 kWh per oven-weekend, versus the standby state burning continuously all weekend. Per SOP-02 and the RF-01 manual, ovens stay on for 30 minutes after the line stops, then must be switched off (and only when no boards are inside) — never left in standby.

## Excess energy in incident S5

During incident S5 (2025-10-17 to 2025-10-20), RF-02 was left in standby all weekend:
- Weekend energy: ~1,556 kWh
- Normal weekend: ~346 kWh
- **Excess: ~1,210 kWh from a single oven**

The off-schedule rule would flag this, but only after 120 minutes above 20% of rating — so the real saving comes from switching the oven off proactively.

## Load Shedding Order (per EM-02 playbook, applied under SOP-03)

**Shed first:** EV charging (EV-01) is the first action — it's paused, shedding 100% of present EV load, because it has no effect on production. [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

The full playbook order (least disruptive first):
1. **Pause EV charging** — EV-01 — 100% [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
2. Delay the next burn-in loading — BI-01, BI-02 — 35% [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
3. Raise chilled-water setpoint +1 °C — CH-01, CH-02 — 4% [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]
4. Lower compressed-air pressure 0.5 bar — AC-01, AC-02, AC-03 — 3.5% [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook]

**Never shed:**
- Server room (DC-01) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Running molders mid-cycle (IM-01 to IM-04) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]
- Reflow ovens with boards inside (RF-01 to RF-03) [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-02_demand_management.md#EM-02 Demand Management > Load-shed playbook > Never shed]

This is reinforced by the energy policy: "The server room, running molders mid-cycle and reflow ovens with boards inside are never shed." [source: docs/knowledge/energy-management/EM-01_energy_policy.md#EM-01 Energy Policy > Operating principles]
